# 2.3 Counting rules, nCr mod p, stars and bars, inclusion–exclusion

Phase 2 (Mathematics I), target rating 1400–1700. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Binomials modulo a prime (`ncr-mod-p`)

Precompute factorials and inverse factorials to answer C(n, r) mod p in O(1).

**Works because:** p is prime and larger than every n used, and n fits in an array.

### Product and sum rules (`product-sum-rules`)

Count arrangements by multiplying independent choices and adding disjoint cases.

**Works because:** The choices are independent (product rule) or the cases do not overlap (sum rule).

### Identical items into distinct boxes (`stars-bars`)

Count ways to split n identical items into k distinct boxes, possibly with lower bounds per box.

**Works because:** Items are indistinguishable and boxes are distinguishable, so a distribution is a placement of k − 1 bars.

### Counting by inclusion–exclusion (`include-exclude`)

Count objects that avoid every one of several bad properties by an alternating sum over sets of properties.

**Works because:** The size of every intersection of bad sets can be computed directly.

### Counting by a bijection (`bijection-paths`)

Map objects to choices of positions (lattice paths, sequences with fixed counts) and count them with one binomial.

**Works because:** There is a one-to-one correspondence between the objects and the subsets being counted.
